title: GPU inventory & commit schedule by region
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a snapshot of physical GPU inventory, committed purchase orders, and an immediate 6-month procurement schedule broken down by region. It is intentionally tactical — used to coordinate order timing, cross-check lead-time exposure, and decide on short-term bursts vs. reserved capacity reallocation.

Executive summary:
- Total physical GPUs (active + queued): 5,240 units across 4 regions.
- Current 30-day burn rate: ~420 GPUs/month (model training + heavy inference experiments), expected to rise to ~520 GPUs/month if Dedicated pipeline activation goes as forecasted.
- Near-term risk: H100 backlog increases lead-time variance to 18–30 weeks for key vendors; contingency recommended via spot-burst partnerships and targeted L4 orders for less-sensitive workloads.

Procurement pipeline (committed orders and in-negotiation):

PO-1230 | A100-80GB | 240 | Secondary | 2026-03-01 | 2026-05 to 2026-06 | 9–13  | us-west1 | purchase-order | contingency order

Capacity runway calc notes:
- monthly_burn_eq_units uses a normalized unit where one H100 counts as 1.0, A100 as 0.7, L4 as 0.25, T4 as 0.05 for throughput-oriented capacity planning.
- runway_weeks = available_pool / (monthly_burn_eq_units / 4.3).
- We model Dedicated reservations separately because they are contractual and cannot be rebalanced quickly.

Risk matrix (short bullets):
- H100 vendor backlog: highest procurement risk; inventory on hand in us-west1 is low runway (7 weeks). Recommend immediate migration of non-latency-critical workloads to A100/L4 where possible.
- Regional imbalance: us-west1 holds a disproportionate H100 fraction; consider transferring 100–150 A100s from us-west1 -> us-east1 to free rack/cooling capacity for H100 in west region.
- Customs & import windows: eu shipments show 1–2 week customs variance; plan 15% extra lead buffer for EU allocations.

Contingency options: (ranked)
1) Short-term cloud bursting with partner accounts (GCP us-west1 and AWS eu-west-1) for up to 6 weeks — estimate 2–3% higher unit cost but immediate capacity.
2) Loaner swaps with Dedicated customers on a time-limited basis (requires legal sign-off).
3) Prioritized model-quantization pilot to reduce H100 demand on critical routes (target 12% token-cost savings).

Open decisions and asks to vendors/purchasing: (action owner in parentheses)
- Confirm feasibility of partial shipments for PO-1192 (Aisha).
- Lock freight-forwarder for EU H100 shipment to guarantee customs window (Diego).
- Approve contingency secondary A100 PO-1230 to cover 8-week shortfall if PO-1192 slips beyond Aug (Finance sign-off needed) (Evelyn).

Short notes on utilization anomalies (observed Apr 2025–Feb 2026):
- Inference fleet utilization spikes around major feature launches (notably November and January) with H100 queue times increasing by 1.6x for large-context jobs.
- Training allocation has been smoothing out due to more aggressive schedule batching but remains bursty month-end.

Suggested next steps (timeline):
- This week: finalize freight forwarder and attempt partial-ship confirmations (owners: Aisha/Diego).
- 2 weeks: run rapid quantization pilots on 3 top consumers to validate 10–15% H100 reduction potential (owner: Applied ML).
- 4 weeks: update committed PO timeline and re-run runway model with new burn projections (owner: Eng infra lead).
